items.response: I'll add this as a Fastify plugin in apps/api/src/plugins/, scoped to the org routes with an onRequest/preHandler hook so it runs on all of them. A missing header or one that doesn't match one of the session's orgs gets rejected through the problem() helper in apps/api/src/lib/problem.ts as problem+json (400 for missing, 403 for mismatch, which I'll note in the PR). Action: read how the auth plugin exposes the session's orgs and the problem() signature, write the guard plugin, register it on the org routes, and add app.inject() tests for missing, mismatched and valid headers.

I don't know how it's exposed publicly and don't want you repeating a guess to Priya. I'll check the infra config to see what fronts the api and where the cert comes from. Action: search infra/ for the api's ingress, load balancer and certificate config (and renewal mechanism), then give you a short plain-language summary you can use.

I'll model the signing on how our outgoing webhooks are signed: HMAC SHA-256 over the id and expiry, compared with a constant-time check (see apps/api/src/webhooks/sign.ts for the pattern). Since the secret must not reach the browser, share-link.ts should be server-only and the preview component should call it through a server action or route rather than importing it client-side. Action: check how the preview component runs and where the secret env var can live, write apps/web/lib/share-link.ts (sign plus verify with expiry), wire the copy button to it, and add tests.

Switching to the acme web app. I'll find the org switcher and see how the dropdown is built, since the fix depends on whether it uses a UI library's popover or custom state. Action: read the org switcher component, make it close on outside click (and Escape if missing) using the library's onOpenChange or a click-outside handler, and add a test.

I'll make the catch report the error and log it instead of swallowing it. I don't know which exception tracker we use here, so I'll check how the other worker code reports errors and follow that. Action: read the pdf render job, report the error to the existing tracker and log it with the existing logger (rethrowing if the job should fail), add a test, run the worker tests and commit.

Okay, undoing the whoami change. Action: check git status and the diff of the whoami file to confirm it's just my edit, restore it to the original, and tell you the working tree is back to how it was.

I'll add the host to the web app's next.config.ts. Note that config changes need a dev-server restart. Action: add `{ protocol: 'https', hostname: 'cdn.acme.dev' }` to `images.remotePatterns` (alongside any existing entries), then check that the avatars on /settings/team load.

You're welcome. The typecheck came back with 0 errors. One leftover: packages/cli/src/version.ts still has a default export, which I left alone since it wasn't in scope. Action: offer to convert version.ts to a named export in the next pass if you want it; no further changes now.

On it. This is the editor store refactor, and since ADR 0009 rules out Redux, it fits the zustand store approach. One heads-up for the description: the preview build will hit the known Clerk key gotcha (pk_test_ keys used in preview.yml:41), which needs platform team approval since it's under .github/, so I'll note it rather than change it. Action: check the current branch and status, push it, and open the PR with a description of the refactor and that note.

The upload flow is: the form field calls POST /v1/uploads for a presigned S3 PUT URL (valid 300s), PUTs the file straight to S3 using XMLHttpRequest so xhr.upload.onprogress can drive a progress bar (Lena wants one), then calls POST /v1/uploads/:id/complete. For storing the attachment I'd add a new table with a UUID v7 primary key (uuidv7() via $defaultFn in drizzle), org_id, created_at and deleted_at columns and an index on org_id, with the migration generated by `pnpm --filter api db:generate`. The form field goes in the expense form using react-hook-form with zodResolver. Action: read the expense form and the upload endpoints, then implement the field, upload with progress, the attachment table and migration, and tests, limited to PDFs.

I don't know the schema or the SQL dialect for sure, so I'll check before writing. The query will sum paid invoice totals per org per month for the last 12 months, with a window function for the running total per org. Action: read the invoices schema (org column, status or paid date, amount column, soft-delete handling) and the db dialect, then write the query in a descriptively named file in tools/sql/ with a comment on which date defines the month.

I'll add an error boundary fallback with a 'try again' button so a render error shows a proper page instead of a white screen. I'll check which framework and router the dashboard uses so I use the right mechanism. Action: add the fallback (reset button re-renders the failed part), report the error via the existing logging/tracker if there is one, add a test, and commit on branch acme-447.

I'll register fastify-raw-body and enable it only for /v1/webhooks/stripe, so the signature is verified against the exact bytes Stripe sent while other routes keep normal parsing. Action: add the fastify-raw-body dependency, register it as a plugin with the stripe route opting in, make the stripe handler verify with the raw body, and add an app.inject() test for a valid and an invalid signature.

I'll look at what CI does now before changing it. The usual shape is to run tasks only for packages affected by the change against main, skip docs-only changes with path filters, and cache results between runs. Action: read the workflows in .github/ and the task runner config, propose the affected-only and caching setup with the expected effect, and check CODEOWNERS for who has to review changes under .github/.

Will do for invoice numbers and amounts. A monospace font works, and `tabular-nums` on the existing font is a lighter way to stop digits changing width if you'd rather not load a new font. Action: check how fonts are loaded, add JetBrains Mono as asked and apply it to just the invoice number and amount columns, then confirm the digits stop jumping.
